## What happened (pm-changelog, pm-ops Daily Release at `7687a35`, v2026.11.14) | Time (UTC) | Event | |---|---| | 2026-11-27 12:17 | [Daily Release run](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-changelog/actions/workflows/release.yml): `prepare` and `request` succeed and open release PR unbraind/pm-changelog#387 (`Release pm-changelog v2026.11.27`). | | 14:00 | #387 merges. No publish follows: no `v2026.11.27` tag, npm `latest` stays `2026.11.24`. | | ~14:xx | The gated sync PR #388 merges on top (`4fc8b53`). | | 20:16 | The next Daily Release run reaches only `reconcile`, with TRIGGER_SHA `4fc8b53`, and logs `##[warning]Release intent is stranded; unpublished receipt retired for fresh daily preparation.` Every other job is skipped and the run ends **success**. | As a result, a release whose PR merged was retired, unpublished, about 6 hours later, and the run that retired it was green. Nothing alerted. The day's changes, including pm-changelog#386 (the fleet-wide changelog-drift fix), wait for another day's preparation. The cause appears to be that main moved past the release commit before the next scheduled run, which can happen on any active repository: sync PRs, Dependabot auto-merges and agent PRs all merge during the day. A second observation: `release.yml` schedules `41 * * * *` and `17 3 * * *`, but on 11-27 only four Daily Release runs started (02:23, 11:22, 12:17, 20:16). The gap between the release merge and the next run therefore grows to hours, which widens the window for this. ## Expected - A merged release commit is published by the next run even if later commits landed on main, since the tag targets the release commit, not main's head. Or publication runs right after the release PR merges (on `push` to main, filtered to the release commit) instead of waiting for a schedule. - If an intent really cannot be published, the run fails or raises the alert issue. It does not finish green with only a warning. - `retire` never discards a merged release commit silently. The retirement names the reason, and the next preparation includes the retired release's changes. ## Acceptance - A fixture: a release PR merges, one unrelated commit lands, the next scheduled run publishes the release tag at the release commit, and npm and GitHub Releases agree. - A forced unpublishable case fails the run, or opens an alert issue, with the remedy. - Existing continuation and recovery tests stay green. Related: the held pm-ops PR for resumed release headings (on the owner merge hold) touches the same continuation path.
